Herb, annual, 5-32 cm high. Flowering stems numerous, scapelike, erect, hollow above, pale green and often tinged red, pilose or glabrous, striate, branched or unbranched, branched in upper half. Rosette leaves few to many, obovate, (0.5)-1.0-9.0 cm long, 0.3-2.0 cm wide, dentate, acute to obtuse, petiole-like attenuate with a winged petiole, puberulous or scabridulous, yellowish green on both surfaces, sometimes tinged purple on upper surface. Synflorescence corymbiform, with 1-3 heads. Peduncle long, apically inflated, glabrous or pilose, without bracts. Heads with 20-50 flowers. Involucre at flowering broadly campanulate, 3.0-6.0 mm long, at flowering (4.0)-7.0-11.0 mm in diameter; involucral bracts oblong-ovate or narrowly ovate, green, glabrous or scaly, minutely ciliate; outer involucral bracts linear or linear-ovate, 1.5-3.0 mm long, c. 0.5 mm wide, acute; inner involucral bracts narrowly ovate, 5.0-6.0 mm long, 1.0-1.5 mm wide, acuminate. Receptacle flat, pitted, without scales. Corolla ligulate, 8.0-9.0 mm long, yellow or sometimes greenish when dry. Achenes obovoid in outline, slightly compressed, 1.5-2.2 mm long, smooth or transversely wrinkled, stramineous, with 8-10 ribs, with 3-5 stronger ribs. Pappus membranous.\r\rBased on: Bobrov, E. G. and Tzvelev, N. N. (ed.) 2000: Flora of the USSR 29, Compositae, Tribe Cichorieae . – Enfield.; Sell, P. D. 1976: 151. Arnoseris Gaertner, 152. Koelpinia Pallas, 153. Hyoseris L., 154. Hedypnois Miller, 155. Rhagadiolus Scop., 156. Aposeris Cass. und 157. Urospermum Scop. – Pp. 306-308 in: Tutin, G. & al. (ed.), Flora Europaea 4. – Cambridge; Sell, P. and Murell, G. 2006: Flora of Great Britain and Ireland 4. – Cambridge; Strother, J. L. 2006: 49. Arnoseris Gaertner und 50. Tolpis Adanson. – Pp. 276-277 in: Flora of North America Editorial Com. (ed.), Flora of North America 19. – New York: Oxford University.\r

Arnoseris minima is a calciphobous annual psammophyte, presumably originating from the Iberian granit regions. Its area (Meusel & Jäger 1992: map 527a) is climatically delimited by summer minimum temperatures in the north and, being winter-green and thus frost-sensitive, by approximately the January isotherm of -2 to -4 °C in the east. The Central European occurrences are largely synanthropous as a weed of cereal crops and due to industrial agriculture and lack of natural habitats close to extirpation.
